items.headline: U.S. Equities Show Modest Gains Mid-Day as Investors Await Key Economic Data and Nvidia Earnings
items.summary: U.S. stock markets are exhibiting modest gains across major indices in mid-day trading today, August 25, 2026. A cautious sentiment prevails as investors look ahead to crucial inflation data later this week and the highly anticipated quarterly earnings report from AI heavyweight Nvidia. Falling oil prices are contributing to an easing of bond market worries and providing some support to equity prices.

items.headline: Moderna surges on positive vaccine trial results
items.summary: Shares of biotech Moderna ($MRNA) climbed 10.5% in early trading following successful late-stage trial results for an experimental personalized mRNA cancer vaccine.

items.headline: Super Micro Computer gains after Cisco partnership
items.summary: Super Micro Computer ($SMCI) gained 8% after Cisco ($CSCO) announced a new partnership to expand its AI infrastructure portfolio.

items.headline: Navitas Semiconductor jumps on acquisition news
items.summary: Navitas Semiconductor ($NVTS) advanced 8% after agreeing to acquire power management solutions provider Claros in a deal valued up to $232.8M, aiming to double its serviceable addressable market for AI data centers.

items.headline: Dick's Sporting Goods tumbles on earnings miss
items.summary: Dick's Sporting Goods ($DKS) cratered 26.1% after the retailer missed Wall Street's second-quarter earnings forecasts and slashed its full-year profit outlook.

items.headline: AST SpaceMobile declines
items.summary: AST SpaceMobile ($ASTS) saw a decline of 9.18% in early trading today.

items.headline: Albemarle slips after JPMorgan price target cut
items.summary: Albemarle ($ALB) shares slipped 5.9% after JPMorgan cut its price target on the specialty chemicals company from $160 to $140 amid reassessments of market conditions and commodity pricing.

items.headline: Technology Stocks Rebound as Energy and Consumer Staples Lag
items.summary: Technology stocks are seeing a rebound today, easing pressure after a mixed trading day on Monday. Meanwhile, the Energy sector is lagging with a 1.35% decline, and Consumer Staples are also down 0.43%. Communication Services and Consumer Discretionary sectors are showing some strength, up 0.48% and 0.39% respectively.

items.headline: Consumer Confidence Weakens, Housing Data Mixed Amid Inflation Watch
items.summary: The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for August decreased by 0.8 points to 89.4, with expectations for the future becoming more pessimistic despite improved assessments of the present situation. The S&P/Case-Shiller Home Price Index for June showed a 1.5% month-over-month improvement but fell in 'real terms' for the thirteenth consecutive month. New Home Sales for July are anticipated to tick down.

items.headline: Fed Officials Look to Jackson Hole for Policy Direction as Inflation Data Looms
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh is expected to deliver a speech at the annual Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium later this week. Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins indicated that a policy tightening would be appropriate soon if evidence of sustained inflation progress does not materialize. Investors are keenly awaiting the release of the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index for July, scheduled for Wednesday, as a key inflation gauge.

items.headline: Nvidia Earnings on Horizon; Dick's Sporting Goods Disappoints
items.summary: All eyes are on chipmaking giant Nvidia ($NVDA), which is scheduled to release its quarterly earnings report after the market close on Wednesday. This report is seen as a crucial test for market risk appetite, particularly concerning the AI trade. In other earnings news, Dick's Sporting Goods ($DKS) reported a significant miss in its second-quarter earnings and cut its full-year profit outlook, leading to a sharp decline in its stock. BMO Financial Group ($BMO) also reported its Q3 results today, with adjusted net income rising 19% year-over-year despite a decrease in reported net income. EHang Holdings ($EH) announced a substantial 203.5% quarter-over-quarter revenue increase in Q2, though its net loss also widened.
